sections.title: Political systems
sections.content:
Key vocabulary for discussing politics:
• democracy — government by the people. Democracy depends on free and fair elections.
• legislation — laws collectively. New legislation was passed to protect the environment.
• bureaucracy — complex administrative procedures. Excessive bureaucracy slows down progress.
• sovereignty — supreme authority over a territory. The nation defended its sovereignty against foreign interference.
• constitution — fundamental laws governing a country. The constitution guarantees freedom of speech.

sections.title: Political actions
sections.content:
Verbs and nouns for political activity:
• campaign — organised effort to achieve a goal. She ran an impressive election campaign.
• lobby — try to influence politicians on an issue. Environmental groups lobby for stricter pollution laws.
• sanction — a penalty imposed on a country. Economic sanctions were imposed to pressure the government.
• ratify — formally approve an agreement. Parliament voted to ratify the trade agreement.

exercises.question: The system of government by elected representatives is:
exercises.explanation: Democracy is a system of government by the whole population through elected representatives.

exercises.question: Complex official rules and procedures are:
exercises.explanation: Bureaucracy is a system of official rules and procedures, often seen as excessive.

exercises.question: To formally approve a treaty or agreement is to:
exercises.explanation: To ratify means to sign or give formal consent to a treaty or agreement.

exercises.question: Penalties imposed on a country to force policy change are:
exercises.explanation: Sanctions are penalties applied by one country against another to force compliance.

exercises.question: The fundamental law of a country is its:
exercises.explanation: A constitution is the fundamental set of principles governing a state.

exercises.question: Trying to influence politicians on a specific issue is to:
exercises.explanation: To lobby means to try to influence a politician on a particular issue.

exercises.question: A country's supreme authority over its territory is its:
exercises.explanation: Sovereignty is the authority of a state to govern itself independently.

exercises.question: Laws passed by a parliament or government body are:
exercises.explanation: Legislation refers to laws that have been enacted by a governing body.
